Split the conjunction and treat the two components independently.

For the first component, view \(q\) as an \(f\)-invariant submodule: the assumption
\[
q\leq \operatorname{comap}(f,q)
\]
says exactly that \(x\in q\Rightarrow f(x)\in q\). Hence every iterate \(f^n(m)\) lies in \(q\). Since evaluating \(p\) at \(f\) and applying it to \(m\) is a finite sum of scalar multiples of these iterates, closure of \(q\) under addition and scalar multiplication gives
\[
(\operatorname{aeval} f\,p)(m)\in q.
\]
This can be formalized by induction on \(p\), or by restricting \(f\) to an endomorphism of \(q\).

For the equivalence, observe that both universally quantified statements are standard consequences of the universal property of \(R[X]\), so prove each unconditionally:

- `aevalTower g y` sends a constant polynomial `C r` to `g r`; therefore its underlying ring hom composed with `Polynomial.C` is the underlying ring hom of `g`.
- Any \(R\)-algebra homomorphism \(\varphi:R[X]\to A\) is evaluation at \(\varphi(X)\), with coefficients sent through `algebraMap`; thus
  \[
  \varphi(p)=\operatorname{eval₂}(\operatorname{algebraMap} R A)(\varphi(X))(p).
  \]

Both identities follow by the polynomial universal property, or equivalently by checking constants and \(X\)/using polynomial induction. The two implications of the `Iff` may then simply discard their hypotheses and invoke the independently established universal identity.
